Most people think it means a cat is happy. And often, it does!
But cats also purr when they're scared, sick, or hurt.
So what is a purr, really?
Deep in a cat's throat is its voice box.
When a cat breathes in and out, tiny parts in there wobble super fast, about twenty five times every second.
Scientists even found tiny soft pads in a cat's voice box that help make such a low sound.
Mother cats purr to their kittens, and kittens purr back. It may help them stay close.
And big cats? Cheetahs can purr. But lions and tigers can't. They roar instead!
So next time a cat purrs on your lap, you'll know there's a tiny buzzing engine inside.
